text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Socialist Edek party is expected to endorse the decision of its leadership to back lawyer Marios Eliades in the presidential elections in 1998.
- Pay disputes at the central abbatoir has forced its closure from today.
- Charalambos Kokkalis, the island's oldest inhabitant, dies at 120.
- President Glafcos Clerides has dismissed reports he took documents to Athens on the upcoming talks with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash next week.
- Police charge four men with conspiracy to murder a gambling club owner gunned down in Larnaca in May.
- Edek, communist Akel party and the centre-left United Democrats are due to take final decisions this week on their cooperation in the elections, after their leaders agreed on a pact last week.

- President Clerides and Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis, who are meeting in Athens today, will discuss tactics that the Greek Cypriot side will follow during the direct talks scheduled to start next week.
- Some 2,313 contract employees in the civil service are waiting for their appointments.
- Hoteliers in the southern port town of Limassol complain of extremely low occupancy levels.
